r-surface.$description:
The corner of a SURFACE: a card, a panel, a sheet, a menu, a dialog.
An alias of the r scale rather than a fresh number, on the same footing as rhythm's
aliases of sp, so the base value cannot drift off the radius scale.

Why the role exists at all: r names how round a corner is, and this names WHICH corner
is being asked about. A manifest that reaches for r-lg has said a length; one that reaches
for r-surface has said a reason, and only the second can be answered differently by an
extension. Re-valuing r-lg to soften a card would soften every unrelated use of the same
step, which is the defect the role tier exists to prevent.

r-control.$description:
The corner of a CONTROL the user presses: a button, an icon button, a chip.
Separate from r-field although both are r.sm today, on the cut that keeps rhythm-group
and dz-stack apart at 12px: same length, different question. An extension that wants pill
buttons over rectangular inputs needs the two to be answerable one at a time.

r-field.$description:
The corner of a FIELD the user types into: an input, a select, a textarea.
The counterpart to r-control, and separate from it for the reason stated there.

bw-surface.$description:
The border of a surface, and therefore Arena's default grouping signal.
This is the single most consequential role in the tier: a hairline says 'these things are
one region' by drawing the region, which is cheap in pixels and correct for dense data.
An extension that sets it to 0px has to make elevation and air carry the grouping instead,
and WCAG 1.4.11 stops being satisfied by the border, which is why removing it is gated
rather than merely allowed.

bw-control.$description:
The border of a pressable control. Distinct from bw-surface because a
button's outline is an affordance, saying where the pressable area ends, while a card's
is a grouping signal. An extension can drop one and keep the other.

bw-field.$description:
The border of a typable field. Distinct again: this one is the boundary
WCAG 1.4.11 measures at 3:1, so it is the border with the least freedom of the three.

shadow-surface-raised.$description:
What a surface rises to when it is hovered, dragged or opened over the page.
An alias of the shadow scale, so the default raised state is exactly the step it
already used. Named for the state rather than the depth so an extension can raise a card
further without every other shadow.2 in the system moving with it.

dur-hover.$description:
How long a hover or press response takes. An alias of dur.fast, which is
what every such transition already spells inline. An extension is where motion energy is
decided, and a duration written as a scale step cannot be re-decided; written as a role
it can, without touching the transitions that are fast for a different reason.

dur-enter.$description:
How long something takes to appear: a menu, a popover, a toast, a dialog.
An alias of dur.mid. Kept apart from dur-hover because an entrance and a hover answer to
different expectations, and an extension that slows one has no reason to slow the other.
